about: Pitch and video numbers, ranked. 'say' is wording the sources support. rank 1-5 = the headline set chosen on 12 Nov 2026. Source ids are in sources.json.

claims.say: About 5 million older Americans who need a grab bar, shower seat or raised toilet seat don't have one, and half of those who need a toilet aid still don't have it four years later.
claims.caveat: Adults 65+ who would clearly benefit. Say 'older Americans', not 'disabled people'.

claims.say: It isn't mainly money: unmet need was higher among younger, healthier older adults. They don't know what to get.
claims.caveat: The paper lists younger age, fewer conditions and no recent hospital stay as predictors; the 'don't know what to get' reading is the authors' explanation (knowledge gaps, stigma, nobody asks).

claims.say: The standard 60-inch turning circle fits fewer than half of wheelchair users for a full turn. So we check against your chair, not a generic number.
claims.caveat: Measured in the US for the Access Board; 495 and 369 users.

claims.say: Fixing hazards at home works: a Cochrane review of 22 trials found 38% fewer falls in people at higher risk. A cheap rails-and-grab-bars programme cut medically treated fall injuries by 26%.
claims.caveat: Only in people selected for risk (no effect in unselected people). No effect on fractures or hospital stays. No trial of an app or a single product.

claims.say: Spotting problems is solved: a CHI 2024 scanner finds them with 86% precision. What nobody does is the next step: which product, what it costs, within your budget.
claims.caveat: ARHAT also suggests design fixes. The gap is specific products, prices, budget and an independent re-check.

claims.say: Even after an occupational therapist visits, only about half of the recommended changes get made. People who believed the change prevents falls were the ones who made it.
claims.caveat: Australian sample of 178 people; old data.

claims.say: 29% of assistive devices end up abandoned; choosing without asking the user predicts it.
claims.caveat: Old US data; newer studies find 14 to 19%.

claims.say: When older adults fitted a rim-mounted (clamp-on) tub rail themselves, 19 of 20 failed a load test.
claims.caveat: Lab study, 20 people. It is why the planner warns on install.

claims.say: Only 18% of contractors called would install a grab bar; the median quote was $394, for a $50 product.
Four in five older adults' falls that reach the ER happen at home; the bedroom, stairs and bathroom each account for about a quarter.
claims.caveat: About half of at-home ER records name no room.

claims.say: A fall in the bathroom is more than twice as likely to cause an injury as one in the living room.
Getting in and out of bed is where 30% of wheelchair-transfer fractures happen in older adults.
18.4 million US adults use a cane, crutches or a walker, against 5.5 million who use a wheelchair.
claims.caveat: Newest Census count; 12 years old, say the year.

claims.say: Phone scans get room shapes right but door sizes wrong more often than you'd think, so the planner flags anything close to a limit for a tape check.
claims.caveat: iPad Pro M4 in 3 spaces; pair it with your own tape-test number.

claims.say: We keep the AI away from measurements: in research, AI-written furniture coordinates did no better than random, while AI rules plus a solver did twice as well.
claims.caveat: Holodeck is a scene-generation benchmark, not accessibility.

do_not_say.say_not: The first app to scan a room for accessibility
The first to suggest fixes from a scan
do_not_say.why: ARHAT, myAccessibleHome and DwellSafe suggest fixes.
The ADA Standards don't apply to private homes; say 'meets the ADA reference width'.

do_not_say.say_not: As accurate as an occupational therapist
do_not_say.why: Even a professional laser scan read by an OT agreed only fairly with an in-person OT on hazards (kappa 0.38).

do_not_say.say_not: This grab bar (or any single product) prevents X% of falls
do_not_say.why: No trial measures a single product.
Cochrane 2023: little or no difference (low certainty).
No home-modification trial in wheelchair users exists.
No study tests RoomPlan door widths against a tape; studies show 2 to 5 cm typical error and doors detected poorly.
